module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 258

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/258](https://www.erdosproblems.com/258)
- [Ch26] P. Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro, [Erdős problem 258](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos258.pdf) (2026)
- [St26] ster-oc, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 258](https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean) (2026)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos258

/--
Let $a_n \to \infty$ be a sequence of non-zero natural numbers. Is
$\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{(a_1 ... a_n)}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

This was proved affirmatively by Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro [Ch26], and formalised in Lean
by ster-oc [St26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean"]
theorem erdos_258 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) →
    Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i)) := by
  sorry


/--
Let $2 \leq a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots$ be a monotone sequence with $a_n \to \infty$.
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{a_1 \cdots a_n}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

Solution: True (proved by Erdős and Straus [ErSt71], Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_258.variants.monotone : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) → Monotone a →
    Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i)) := by
  sorry


/--
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where $t ≥ 2$ is an integer.

Solution: True (proved by Erdős, see Erdős Problems website)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-lean-erdos249-257/blob/a9104f2f12aa0d4e9da8a93574b14990ed02dc2a/adapters/FormalConjecturesAdapter.lean#L109-L117"]
theorem erdos_258.variants.constant : answer(True) ↔ ∀ t ≥ (2 : ℕ),
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / t^(n + 1))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos258

findings.description: The docstring cites “[ErSt71], Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13”, but there is no Theorem 2.13 in that paper. Equation (2.13) is an inequality within the proof of Lemma 2.2. The monotone irrationality result is Theorem 2.23, obtained from Lemmas 2.2 and 2.14. The Lean statement itself is mathematically sound.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Straus, Some number theoretic results, pp. 640–641: (2.13) concludes the proof of Lemma 2.2; Theorem 2.23 states that series (2.1) is irrational whenever 2 ≤ a₁ ≤ a₂ ≤ ⋯. https://msp.org/pjm/1971/36-3/pjm-v36-n3-p07-s.pdf
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the citation with “[ErSt71], Theorem 2.23”, optionally mentioning its constituent Lemmas 2.2 and 2.14.

status_issues.recorded: An unconditional `formal_proof using lean4` annotation points to [St26]; the docstring likewise says the result was formalised in Lean.
status_issues.source_status: The mathematical problem is solved affirmatively, but the linked Lean proof only formalises the deduction from an assumed Tao–Teräväinen theorem. It is not a complete unconditional formal proof.
status_issues.evidence: The exact linked gist explicitly declares `axiom tao_teravainen` at lines 311–314 and says that this theorem is “stated here without proof”. Its final `erdos_258` uses this axiom through `tao_teravainen_divisors_le`. The unconditional mathematical result is supported by [Ch26], Theorem 2, and the #258 remark in Tao–Teräväinen, arXiv:2512.01739v2.
status_issues.suggested_change: Keep `research solved` and `answer(True)`. Remove the unconditional formal-proof annotation, or qualify it as a conditional formal proof assuming a declaration of the Tao–Teräväinen input. Clarify the same qualification in the docstring until a complete formal proof is linked.

reformulations.difference: Lean requires a n ≥ 2 at every natural index, whereas [Ch26] allows arbitrary positive integers a₁,a₂,… tending to infinity.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given a positive sequence a tending to infinity, set b n = max 2 (a n). Then b satisfies Lean’s hypotheses and agrees with a eventually. Choose N beyond all differences, and let Q_a(N)=∏_{i=1}^N a_i and similarly Q_b(N). Beyond N, the summands for a are Q_b(N)/Q_a(N) times those for b. Consequently S(a)=c·S(b)+r with nonzero rational c and rational r, so their irrationality is equivalent. The converse restriction is immediate, and a₀ never enters the series. Proved independently in /workspace/review/convergence.lean as Review258.positive_iff_ge_two; its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

reformulations.difference: Theorem 2.23 of Erdős–Straus covers all nondecreasing sequences with a₁ ≥ 2. The file separates the case tending to infinity from the constant-base case in .variants.constant.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A nondecreasing natural-valued sequence either tends to infinity or is eventually constant. In the latter case, its series differs from the corresponding constant-base series by a nonzero rational scaling and a rational finite-prefix correction. Thus the two variants together are equivalent to the full monotone theorem. This conjunction equivalence was proved as Review258.monotone_full_iff_parts in /workspace/review/convergence.lean, without using any admitted problem statement.

review.notes: All three mathematical statements were checked; no mathematical misformalization was found. Lean experiments verified real-valued division, indexing, positive denominators, satisfiable hypotheses, and summability. The constant-case link states exactly the repository proposition; its 12-file dependency closure contains no custom axioms or proof placeholders. The external proofs were not rebuilt under their original toolchains. erdosproblems.com/258 and its forum returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so the mathematical claims and solved status were checked against the primary papers and cited proof files instead. Scratch checks and equivalence proofs are under /workspace/review/.
